pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This recently bit us when quotas for a resource in a non-core group exceeded what we thought to be our configured limit. We were not applying count limits properly (leaving off the group for non-core resources) and did not have any feedback that our quotas were misformatted.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #97765

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
Add a very specific validation rule to fail the resource quotas creation and update request: count/<resource>.<group> for resources from non-core groups or count/<resource> for resources from the core group
```

This looks like it is changing validation on existing data, which is not backwards compatible. 

/hold

standard questions when we want to tighten validation:
* does it prevent a no-op update of existing persisted objects that would fail this new validation? (would block storage migration tasks)
* does it prevent deletion of existing persisted objects with finalizers that would fail this new validation? (update is required to remove finalizers to allow deletion)
* does it prevent controllers from updating status of existing persisted objects that would fail this new validation?

we could consider ratcheting validation:
* apply this tightened validation on create
* apply this tightened validation on update where the old object passed this validation (don't let a valid object become invalid)
* skip this tightened validation on update where the old object fails this validation

c.f. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/59984

issue_context.title: Object count quotas API has sharp edges
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
Validation of object count quotas would help prevent misuse. The syntax is currently `count/<resource>.<group>` for non-core groups, meaning a count quota like `count/jobs` or `count/deployments` will be accepted but have no effect.

**Why is this needed**:
This recently bit us when quotas for a resource in a non-core group exceeded what we thought to be our configured limit. We were not applying count limits properly (leaving off the group for non-core resources) and did not have any feedback that our quotas were misformatted.
comments: a very specific validation rule to fail the resourcequota creation request for count/jobs or count/deployments are surely helpful to avoid the misconfigure issue you mentioned.

review_comments: helper.IsStandardQuotaResourceName seems to contain incomplete set of resources in core group, e.g. serviceaccount. this means count/serviceaccount would not be allowed with this PR, but it is ligit.

@yliaog you're right.

`serviceaccounts ` and `limitranges` are not in  [standardQuotaResources](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/apis/core/helper/helpers.go#L194). 

```shell
➜  ~ kubectl api-resources --api-group="" --namespaced
NAME                     SHORTNAMES   APIVERSION   NAMESPACED   KIND
bindings                              v1           true         Binding
configmaps               cm           v1           true         ConfigMap
endpoints                ep           v1           true         Endpoints
events                   ev           v1           true         Event
limitranges              limits       v1           true         LimitRange
persistentvolumeclaims   pvc          v1           true         PersistentVolumeClaim
pods                     po           v1           true         Pod
podtemplates                          v1           true         PodTemplate
replicationcontrollers   rc           v1           true         ReplicationController
resourcequotas           quota        v1           true         ResourceQuota
secrets                               v1           true         Secret
serviceaccounts          sa           v1           true         ServiceAccount
services                 svc          v1           true         Service
```
I will add `serviceaccounts` and `limitranges ` together to `standardQuotaResources ` in this pr later.

what about bindings and endpoints? and events or podtemplates? i think if they are allowed currently for quota, they should be allowed after your PR is merged.

it may be safer by checking "StandardQuotaResourceName + a few additional resources" here.

this would allow specifying quota with just 'serviceaccounts', in addition to 'count/serviceaccounts'. could you check if it works as intended? i.e. create a quota with the following spec, create a new service account, see if it would be blocked due to exceeding quota.

spec:
  hard:
    serviceaccounts: "1"
add a comment about why it is invalid?
